collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Children interview their relatives about ordinary life and draw the village they want: show the elders, or keep collecting.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) have spent a season asking every grown-up what life was like when they were young: what they ate, what they played, what they were scared of. They have also drawn the village they want when they grow up. It has a slide down the hill. What should they do with it all?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The children present it all at the gathering. The elders learn things about each other they never knew. The slide down the hill is built, briefly, until someone ends up in the stream.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The children keep going for another year, until they have a story from every hut. Then they give it to the oldest villager, who reads it all in one night and says it is the best history of Isola ever made.
